hook.text: The producer emits events 10x faster than the consumer can process them. The buffer fills. What happens next?

buildup.text: Without backpressure, the system crashes — out of memory, dropped events, or cascading failures.

discovery.text: Backpressure signals the producer to slow down when the consumer can't keep up.

twist.text: Kafka handles this implicitly: slow consumers just fall behind. But lag can grow into a permanent backlog.

climax.text: Monitoring consumer lag is essential. If it only grows, you need more consumers or slower producers.

punchline.text: If you can't keep up, say so. That's backpressure.

quiz.question: What is backpressure in a streaming system?
options: A signal for the producer to slow down when the consumer can't keep up
A way to speed up consumers
